turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): alright, in you come. i grabbed your obs just now. blood pressure's one twenty eight over seventy eight, and the pulse was eighty... nah, seventy six.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): oh, okay. um, i legged it up from the car park, so i thought the pulse might be up, i always rush and then worry i've wrecked the reading.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): it's a sitting one, you're right. temp thirty six point six, oxygen ninety eight percent, resps sixteen.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): thanks for that. i'm dr ellison. what's brought you in?

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): it's my tummy, mainly the cramps. they grab low down, left or across the middle, and once i've been to the loo they ease off. i've got notes in my phone, half of them just say felt awful, if you want the ramble.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): talk me through it. how long have the cramps been going?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): err, i want to say last winter, or maybe the winter before, i cannot land on a month. i nearly said eight months, but no, it's a year, a full year, i was already uncomfortable at christmas.

[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): she's not exaggerating, i hear it every night. i only moved in in june, after i did my own back, slipped a disc picking up my little one, so i'm on the couch till physio clears me.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): a year of cramps that settle after a bowel motion. what else is the gut doing?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): bloating is the other one. by mid arvo i look six months pregnant, unfortunate joke, and the work pants don't do up, then it eases overnight if i lie on my left. bowels swing the other way too. constipated two or three days, hard little bits, straining, then it flips to loose stools, three times before lunch, urgent, messy, not quite water.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): so constipation and loose stools taking turns, with the bloating. what sets the cramps off?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): stress, and a big pasta lunch, or onion. i cut onion for four days, a very half baked experiment, and it was a bit better, then a team lunch undid it. work is hideous, i'm in payroll at the hospital, new system, there till seven most nights, and the cramps love a deadline.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): mm. and the cramp goes every time you pass stool, or only sometimes?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): every time, pretty much, within a few minutes. if nothing comes out it just sits there, hot and gripey, and the spreadsheets can wait. sorry, too much detail again.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): detail's what i need. any blood in the stool?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): no. none. i check the paper and the bowl, because a woman on my team had bowel cancer last year and i got spooked. no blood.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): and your weight. lost any without trying?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): no. haven't lost any. i weigh in on sundays and i'm the same as this time last year, give or take a kilo that wanders.
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): she eats pretty normally. i'm the one on toast, bending to cook sets my back off. that's me, not her.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): any vomiting, or fevers with this?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): no vomiting. no fevers either, i haven't felt hot or shivery, just the gut doing its thing.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): waterworks? stinging, or going more often?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): no, all normal. no stinging, usual amount. i do drink a lot of tea, about six cups, which maybe stirs the bowel, i haven't proved that.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): what medicines are you on, chemist stuff included?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): buscopan. i thought they were ten milligrams, but i looked at the box this morning, they're twenty milligrams, one three times a day when the cramps are bad. swallowed, not the injection or anything.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): and i bought metamucel, the orange tin, took it twice last month, bloated me worse, so i stopped. coloxyl too, two at night, i was going to say a fortnight but it was one week, then i stopped. didn't help.
[SEG0027] person_4 (CAREGIVER): buscopan's in the kitchen drawer, i don't touch it. my tablets are the naproxen they gave me for my back. different bottle entirely.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): right, so buscopan twenty milligrams up to three times a day, and the fibre and the softener are finished. any other regular medicine?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): no. no vitamins even. uh, a coworker swears by magnesium and i keep meaning to start, but i haven't bought it.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): i'll have a feel of your tummy. hop up on the bed for me.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): yep. jeans are tight from today's bloating, one second. breakfast was a banana and a coffee, and coffee is a trigger some days and not others, which makes the diary annoying.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): abdomen's soft, bowel sounds are present. tender low on the left, no masses, and no guarding.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah, that left bit twinges when you press. bruised, not stabbing. i can live with that.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): thinking it through, cramps easing after stool, bloating, bowels flipping for a year, no bleeding, weight steady, only a bit tender. i'm leaning towards irritable bowel.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): mechanism-wise, the nerves in the bowel get oversensitive. gas or stool stretching it, or stress from work, sets off a spasm, that's the cramp, and once the stool passes the spasm lets go. the bowel lining isn't damaged. working impression, not signed off.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): so not cancer. i've been on my phone at two in the morning reading, then i can't sleep, and the next day the gut is worse, which sort of matches.
[SEG0037] person_4 (CAREGIVER): phone glowing at midnight, i've told her. my sister did the same after a mole scare, didn't sleep for a month. different person, not her family.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): the late scrolling won't help. we'll still do bloods so we're not just guessing. full blood count, crp, coeliac screen, and thyroid function.
[SEG0039] person_1 (NURSE): i can take the bloods straight after, if the form's on the system. collection's quiet.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): yes please. i'll send the request now, so the bloods are booked for today once we're done.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): today suits me. parking is a nightmare and i don't want a second trip, i've already shuffled my spreadsheets to be here.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): food-wise i'm not starting a strict diet. keep a simple diary for two weeks, ease off onion and the big pasta meals, and cut the tea back from those six cups. regular meals, and ease the coffee if you find it sets you off.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): cutting the tea will hurt, but i can try. i'll make the diary too detailed, times and stool type. is the bristol chart the picture one? i printed it and it caused a domestic on the fridge.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): the chart's fine, don't chase perfect notes. if the bloods fit irritable bowel we stick with diet, the buscopan you already take, and whatever you can do about the late finishes. not a new tablet for every symptom.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): the finishes aren't mine to change till go-live, but i can stop eating at the desk. um, do i keep the buscopan the same?
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): yes. twenty milligram tablets, one up to three times a day when it cramps. leave the coloxyl and the metamucil off unless we revisit them.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): got it. and if something changes, say i actually saw blood, i shouldn't wait, should i? i like the rule written out, otherwise i'll talk myself out of calling.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): blood, weight dropping off, waking from sleep to open your bowels, or pain that's severe, you contact us sooner, don't wait. otherwise i'll see you in two weeks to go over the results.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): two weeks, i'll put it in the phone now, otherwise it vanishes. i missed a dental check in, irrelevant, ignore me.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): reception'll book it as you leave. we'll see if this impression still holds once the numbers are back.
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): come with me after and i'll get those tubes done. won't be long.

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient cannot date when the cramps began, only placing them around a previous winter while stating the duration is a year.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

bad.reason: She mentions not sleeping after late-night phone reading; neurological category/current certainty not clearly established as symptom.
bad.text: Difficulty sleeping (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Constipation is described as hard little stools with straining, and loose stools are urgent and messy/not quite watery.
Abdominal cramps are triggered/worsened by stress, a big pasta lunch, and onion.
Coffee is also a possible trigger on some days.
No other regular medicines, including no vitamins; magnesium has not been started despite considering it.
Metamucil was only taken twice last month and was stopped because it made bloating worse.
Planned blood tests were to be done today/straight after the consultation, with the request sent during the visit.
Red-flag advice included contacting the clinic sooner if waking from sleep to open the bowels.
